title: 非洲的大型野生动物该被猎杀吗?(2)
desc: 非洲的大型野生动物该被猎杀吗?(2)

paragraphs.en: In a sense, the hunters are part of an ancient tradition of sport hunting that stretches back thousands of years: generations of emperors, kings, aristocracy, later merchants and other newly monied classes, all of whom have sought to prove themselves, satisfy primal urges, test their mettle or find spiritual fulfilment in the act of hunting.
paragraphs.zh: 从某种意义上来说，猎手们所延续的是一项传承了数千年的游猎传统：一代又一代的帝王、君主、贵族，再到后来的商人和其他新晋富裕阶层，都曾借狩猎证明自我、释放原始本能、磨炼胆识或是寻求精神上的满足。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps perversely, hunting cultures have been forced to carefully conserve their wildlife: allowing animal numbers to rebound enables future massacres.
paragraphs.zh: 或许有些矛盾的是，狩猎文化反倒促使人们不得不用心保护野生动物：让动物种群数量得以恢复，才能保障日后可持续的猎杀。

paragraphs.en: Many of the best and longest-preserved regions around the world were first brought under environmental protection for the enjoyment of a bloodthirsty elite.
paragraphs.zh: 世界上许多保存最为完好、存续时间最长的荒野区域，最初正是为了满足嗜血权贵的享乐需求，才被划入环境保护范围。

paragraphs.en: The Bialowieza forest, for example, often celebrated as one of Europe's last unspoiled "primeval" woodlands, was set aside as a hunting park for Polish kings in the 15th century.
paragraphs.zh: 例如比亚沃维耶扎森林，常被称作欧洲现存为数不多未遭破坏的“原始”林地之一，它早在15世纪就被划为波兰国王的狩猎苑。

paragraphs.en: In medieval Europe such reserves were known as "forests", whether or not they were wooded, and were governed under the separate code of "forest law".
paragraphs.zh: 在中世纪的欧洲，这类保护区一律被称作“猎苑”，无论园内是否覆盖林木，并且受独立的《猎苑法》管辖。

paragraphs.en: These were privileged, private domains closed to scrutiny and far from prying eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 它们属于享有特权的私人领地，隔绝外界审视，远离众人窥探的目光。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes they were sites of discreet deal-making and diplomacy.
paragraphs.zh: 有时这里也是一些隐秘交易与外交磋商的场所。

paragraphs.en: What happened in the forest, in other words, stayed in the forest.
paragraphs.zh: 换句话说，林中发生的一切，就留在林中。

paragraphs.en: The creation of hunting preserves had the secondary outcome of conserving large tracts of wild or wild-like habitat.
paragraphs.zh: 设立狩猎保护区，也附带产生了一个结果：大片荒野或近似荒野的栖息地得以留存。

paragraphs.en: "If we understand conservation as conscious short-term restraint for long-term benefit," the historian Thomas Allsen has argued, "then many of the most active conservationists in history were political elites, the royal hunters and the polities they controlled."
paragraphs.zh: 历史学家托马斯·奥尔森曾提出：“倘若我们将保护理解为出于长远利益而做出短期的主动克制，那么历史上最积极的一批自然保护者，恰恰是政治权贵、王室猎手以及他们所掌控的政权。”

paragraphs.en: After disastrous collapses in African animal populations under colonial rule, European imperial powers imposed the only model of wildlife preservation they knew: a patchwork of private hunting preserves, implanting feudal principles into a new context.
paragraphs.zh: 殖民统治时期非洲野生动物数量遭遇灾难性锐减之后，欧洲列强推行了他们唯一熟知的野生动物保护模式：一片又一片私人狩猎保护区，将封建制度的治理逻辑移植到全新的土地之上。

paragraphs.en: Since 1900, about 1.4m sq km of sub-Saharan Africa have been set aside for trophy hunting.
paragraphs.zh: 自1900年以来，撒哈拉以南非洲大约已有140万平方公里的土地被划为战利品狩猎区。

paragraphs.en: Many of Africa's best-known wilderness areas and national parks were initially protected for the benefit of hunters.
paragraphs.zh: 非洲许多家喻户晓的荒野地带与国家公园，最初设立的初衷都是服务于猎手。

paragraphs.en: South Africa's beloved Kruger national park began life as the Sabi and Singwitzi game reserves, and though hunting within the park is now banned, even today it shares unfenced boundaries with trophy-hunting estates, so that the same animals, safeguarded one minute, may pass over an invisible line and become fair game the next.
paragraphs.zh: 南非备受喜爱的克鲁格国家公园，最早只是萨比与辛维茨狩猎保护区；尽管如今园内已经禁止狩猎，但它至今仍与多处战利品狩猎庄园没有围栏相隔。于是，上一秒还受保护的动物，只要跨过这条看不见的边界，下一秒就会成为合法的猎杀目标。

paragraphs.en: Big-game hunters were the originators of the international conservation movement and continue to finance, to a surprising extent, wilderness preservation in Africa and North America.
paragraphs.zh: 大型猎物猎手正是国际自然保护运动的发起者，时至今日，他们仍在相当大程度上出资资助非洲与北美洲的荒野保护工作。

paragraphs.en: But they built it based on a central contradiction: that one might save wildlife by killing it.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，这套保护体系建立在一个核心矛盾之上：人们可以通过猎杀野生动物来拯救它们。

paragraphs.en: Trophy hunting, especially of rare or endangered species, is a highly emotive and divisive issue, and there have been many attempts to ban it.
paragraphs.zh: 战利品狩猎，尤其是捕猎稀有或濒危物种，是一个极易引发情绪争议、立场分化的话题，已有不少人试图将其取缔。

paragraphs.en: But so closely entangled is it with African conservation, it's not clear they can be separated and survive.
paragraphs.zh: 但这项产业已经和非洲的野生动物保护深度绑定，目前尚不清楚二者分开之后，是否还能够各自存续。

paragraphs.en: Paul Stones is a professional hunter, a "PH", as it is known colloquially.
paragraphs.zh: 保罗·斯通斯是一名职业猎手，业内俗称“PH”。

paragraphs.en: The PH is a breed of white African men trained to nanny their wealthy clients through the African bush.
paragraphs.zh: 这类职业猎手大多是在非洲生活的白人男性，他们受过专门训练，带着富有的客户穿行于非洲丛林，全程提供照料引导。

paragraphs.en: Stones himself is tall, tanned, with a relentless Boy Scout energy and a highly developed ability to adapt his manner to his company.
paragraphs.zh: 斯通斯本人身材高大、皮肤黝黑，永远有着童子军一般充沛的精力，并且十分擅长根据身边人的身份调整自己的言行举止。

paragraphs.en: He will take the amateur gun enthusiast, harry or encourage him through rough terrain, hand him a bottle of cold water when he overheats, then place him in the precise spot he needs to be to pull the trigger.
paragraphs.zh: 他会带着业余狩猎爱好者艰难跋涉于崎岖地带，不断催促或是鼓励对方；当客户酷热难耐时递上一瓶冰水，再把客户带到扣动扳机所需的精准位置。

paragraphs.en: On the hunt I attended, Stones' client was fairly typical, demographically speaking: white, American, Republican.
paragraphs.zh: 就人口特征而言，我参与的这次狩猎里，斯通斯的客户十分典型：白人、美国人、共和党人。

paragraphs.en: The client (whom I agreed not to identify; let's call him Elmer) was fit for his age and spoke with a gentle southern drawl.
paragraphs.zh: 这位客户（我已答应不透露其真实身份，我们暂且称他埃尔默）以他的年纪来说身体健壮，说话带着温和的美国南方拖腔。

paragraphs.en: He was a Christian man, whose wife of many years preferred to stay at home.
paragraphs.zh: 他是一名基督徒，相伴多年的妻子更愿意留在家中。

paragraphs.en: I could see why.
paragraphs.zh: 我能理解其中缘由。

paragraphs.en: We were sleeping in spartan army-style tents, albeit tents with plumbed-in toilets behind bamboo screens out back.
paragraphs.zh: 我们睡在简陋的军用帐篷里，只不过帐篷后方隔着竹制屏风设有带管道供水的卫生间。

paragraphs.en: Still, Elmer was paying plenty for the pleasure of being there.
paragraphs.zh: 即便如此，埃尔默还是为这次狩猎付出了高昂的费用。

paragraphs.en: The basic cost for a buffalo hunt was $2,150 (￡1,590) a day, for a minimum of 10 days.
paragraphs.zh: 猎杀一头水牛的基础费用为每天2150美元（折合1590英镑），最低狩猎时长十天。

paragraphs.en: Add to that the charter of the bush plane we flew in on ($5,500 at the time), as well as gun and other hunting permits (upwards of $1,000 a head).
paragraphs.zh: 除此之外，还有我们乘坐丛林飞机往返的包机费用（当时为5500美元），枪支以及各类狩猎许可费用（每人1000美元起）。

paragraphs.en: Then there were the game fees.
paragraphs.zh: 之后还有猎物费。

paragraphs.en: When you shoot an animal in Mozambique, as in many African countries, you must pay a predetermined sum.
paragraphs.zh: 在莫桑比克以及许多非洲国家，你猎杀一头动物就必须缴纳一笔事先定好的费用。

paragraphs.en: Stones offers the menu on his website: impalas ($600) and warthogs ($700) are the bargain basement.
paragraphs.zh: 斯通斯在他的网站上列出了收费清单：黑斑羚（600美元）和疣猪（700美元）属于价格最低的一档。

paragraphs.en: He could arrange for you to shoot a crocodile or even a hippopotamus, if you so wish, for a mere $5,800.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你愿意，他也可以安排你猎杀一条鳄鱼，甚至一头河马，收费仅5800美元。

paragraphs.en: A leopard – currently classed as "vulnerable" by the International Union for Conservation of Nature - Will set you back $11,650.
paragraphs.zh: 一头豹子——目前被国际自然保护联盟列为“易危”物种——猎杀费用就要11650美元。

paragraphs.en: A lion? $25,000. Lions, Stones noted drily, are "not something you dish out like doughnuts".
paragraphs.zh: 狮子呢？25000美元。斯通斯冷淡地说道，狮子可不是“甜甜圈一样随手就能拿的东西”。

paragraphs.en: In this particular section of the reserve, or hunting block, there were four lions available to hunt every year, an estimated 2% to 4% of the local population.
paragraphs.zh: 在保护区的这一片狩猎区块，每年仅有四头狮子可供猎杀，大约占到当地狮子种群数量的2%?4%。

paragraphs.en: But one does not simply shoot a lion if it crosses your path.
paragraphs.zh: 可就算一头狮子出现在你面前，你也不能直接开枪猎杀。

paragraphs.en: Lion hunts are highly choreographed, rarefied affairs; you're looking at $70,000 before you even load your rifle.
paragraphs.zh: 猎狮是一套流程繁复、门槛极高的活动；甚至在你还没给步枪装上子弹的时候，花费就已经达到7万美元。

paragraphs.en: Then there are the game fees for the bait you'll need - a zebra, warthog and a kudu, say - and for the lion itself.
paragraphs.zh: 除此之外，还要支付用作诱饵的猎物费用——比如一头斑马、一头疣猪和一只捻角羚，再加上狮子本身的猎物费。

paragraphs.en: All in, you're looking at a six-figure outlay with no guarantee that you'll come home with a lion skin for a rug.
paragraphs.zh: 全部算下来，总开销达到六位数，而且你并不能保证最后一定能带着一张狮子皮地毯回家。

paragraphs.en: (Taxidermy not included.)  Elmer has hunted all over Africa, with varying success.
paragraphs.zh: （动物标本制作费用另算。）埃尔默曾在非洲各地狩猎，战果时好时坏。

paragraphs.en: The worst, he said, was in Tanzania, where there were more snares than animals.
paragraphs.zh: 他说最糟糕的一次经历是在坦桑尼亚，那里的捕猎陷阱比野生动物还要多。

paragraphs.en: Other places might have good hunting, sure, but there were people everywhere.
paragraphs.zh: 有些地方狩猎条件固然不错，可到处都是人。

paragraphs.en: He said it again: everywhere.
paragraphs.zh: 他又重复了一遍：到处都是人。

paragraphs.en: You'd be stalking a buffalo for hours, in total silence.
paragraphs.zh: 你可能会屏息潜行数小时追踪一头水牛。

paragraphs.en: Then a man would come by on his bicycle.
paragraphs.zh: 然后就有一个人骑着自行车路过。

paragraphs.en: When you lifted your gun to shoot, he said, you had to think: where's the school?
paragraphs.zh: 当你举枪准备射击的时候，你就得开始顾虑：附近的学校在哪里？

paragraphs.en: By contrast, Niassa – a troubled corner of Africa, where conservancies financed by hunters might the best-resourced operations around – this was where you came for pure experience.
paragraphs.zh: 与之相比，尼亚萨——非洲一处局势动荡的角落，由猎人出资扶持的保护项目或许已是当地资源最充足的保护机构——正是你追求纯粹狩猎体验的去处。

paragraphs.en: The old-style, Hemingway safari.
paragraphs.zh: 那种海明威笔下老式风格的丛林游猎。
